sara: quick heads-up — ran a stacked perf pass on the host path during the spike and seeing ~30-60us extra per request that isn't explained by decode or GPU time. looks host-side. :thinking_face:
ken: can you paste the flame output? is it tokenize, parse, or grpc write path?
jiayi: initial glance — tokenization + grpc small writes. writev syscall is getting hit a lot for tiny frames. also a tiny memcpy in preparse shows up.
sara: flame attached (snippet):
```
samples  flat  cum   function
120     25%   25%   tokenize_batch
80      17%   42%   grpc_writev
40      8%    50%   preparse::parse_request_headers
```
```
# perf record + pyflame, trimmed
```
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./host-proxy --canary
flamegraph.pl perf.data > flame.svg
```
ken: thanks. two quick ideas: 1) async tokenization worker pool so ingress thread returns faster, 2) coalesce small writev into one big iovec per stream chunk. both low-risk.
oliver: also check KV cache hotpath — if an early KVCACHE miss triggers extra header parsing we might be doing redundant tokenization. saw a pattern where the first call to kvcache lookup is sync and blocks.
mike: i dug into grpc framing — when payload < 512B we send four small frames because of our current chunker. if we bump chunk size to 1k for http2 and grpc it halves writev frequency but could impact latency for tiny payloads. experiment suggestion: A/B 512B vs 1k chunking on p99.
sara: can we get concrete numbers? i ran a microbench: 10k requests, single host, no GPU, measuring ingress latency. results:
- baseline (512B chunk): median 4.3ms, p95 12.1ms, p99 45.8ms
- coalesce writev (1k chunk): median 3.9ms, p95 9.6ms, p99 30.2ms
- async token pool + coalesce: median 3.1ms, p95 7.4ms, p99 22.9ms
(so big wins at tail)
jiayi: nice. what's the CPU overhead? if async thread pool just shifts CPU to worker cores it's ok, but we need to watch context switches.
ken: sampled CPU: async + coalesce increased CPU by ~6% overall but reduced tokens decoded on host by 28% because we avoid repeated preprocessing.
infra-bot: deploy-canary: hostside-token-pool v2 -> infra-canary-07 started at 2026-03-18T14:22:03Z :rocket:
sara: another caveat — kernel selection in the runtime can amplify this: when kernel chooses low-latency single-token path we might have more frequent host calls (KV loads) vs batched kernel that relies on continuous streaming. need to ensure batching heuristics prefer keeping a small window open to amortize host overhead.
mike: agree. propose heuristic tweak: if sequence length <= 64 and request_rate > X, prefer kernel variant K2 that does small-block batching for 10ms to gather coalescing. config prototype:
```
batcher {
  max_delay_ms: 10
  min_batch_size: 4
  preferred_kernel: K2_small_block
}
```
jiayi: watch out for latency-sensitive customers — add a route override flag so we don't add delay for premium SLA clients.
oliver: on KV cache behavior: found a race where concurrent lookups for the same key lead to duplicate fetches from persistent store which results in double preparse cost. put in a singleflight dedupe and it eliminated ~12% of tokenization work. patch PR#7891.
sara: great. next steps: 1) keep canary running for 24h, capture tail latencies and CPU. 2) run kernel-batching A/B with small-window param. 3) merge singleflight kvcache dedupe and measure.
ken: i'll own kernel batching A/B — will add metric for "host-overhead-us" and tag by kernel_variant.
mike: i'll instrument writev counts per-request and add a histogram for iovec counts in the proxy. quick grafana panel idea: host_overhead_us split by tokenization | grpc_write | preparse.
jiayi: testing note: when running wrk/vegeta do not use HTTP keepalive=0 — it inflates overhead. use long-lived connections to measure steady-state.
sara: TL;DR: small wins add up — coalescing + async token pool + kvcache dedupe cut p99 by ~50% in microbench. canary is up. please react with :thumbsup: if you're ok with rolling to staging after 24h, otherwise comment. :eyes:
